title: Ext groups computed by an injective resolution of the second argument
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $M,N$ be objects of $\mathcal A$, and let $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(M,N)=\Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],N[0][i])$ ($i\ge0$) be the Ext groups of [def-pc-ext]. Let $N\to I^\bullet$ be an injective resolution of $N$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: a cochain complex $I^\bullet$ of injective objects of $\mathcal A$ with $I^n=0$ for $n<0$, together with a morphism $\varepsilon:N\to I^0$ such that $0\to N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\xrightarrow{d^0}I^1\xrightarrow{d^1}I^2\to\cdots$ is exact. Let $\Hom_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet)$ be the cochain complex of abelian groups with $\Hom_{\mathcal A}(M,I^n)$ in degree $n$ (zero for $n<0$) and differential $f\mapsto d^n\circ f$, and $H^i(\Hom_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet))=\{f:M\to I^i\mid d^i\circ f=0\}/\{d^{i-1}\circ g\mid g:M\to I^{i-1}\}$ its $i$-th cohomology group (for $i=0$ the denominator is $0$). Then for every $i\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of abelian groups

$$
\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(M,N)\;\cong\;H^i\bigl(\Hom_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet)\bigr),
$$

which sends the class of a cocycle $f:M\to I^i$ to the composite $M[0]\xrightarrow{f}I^\bullet[i]\xleftarrow{\ \varepsilon[i]\ }N[0][i]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$, where $f$ is read as a morphism of complexes $M[0]\to I^\bullet[i]$ and $\varepsilon:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence invertible in $D(\mathcal A)$. In particular, when $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives, $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(M,-)$ is the classical $i$-th right derived functor $R^i\Hom_{\mathcal A}(M,-)$ computed by injective resolutions, and the right-hand side does not depend on the choice of the resolution.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 06XR (derived-lemma-compute-ext-resolutions, line 8682), part (1): $\Ext^i_{\mathcal A}(X^\bullet,Y^\bullet)=\Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(X^\bullet,I^\bullet[i])$ for an injective resolution $Y^\bullet\to I^\bullet$, applied to $X^\bullet=M[0]$, $Y^\bullet=N[0]$; morphisms of $K(\mathcal A)$ from $M[0]$ to $I^\bullet[i]$ are the cocycles $M\to I^i$ modulo $d^{i-1}\circ g$.
